q.description: YNAB's search: comma-separated terms that must all match, each free text (payee, category, memo or account name, or an exact amount) or one of `Payee:`, `Category:` (`Category: Split` for splits), `Memo:`, `Account:`, `Flag:` (a color, its name or None), `Is:` (Uncleared, Cleared, Reconciled, Unreconciled, Cleared or Reconciled), `Outflow:`/`Inflow:` (`25`, `>=25`, `<=25`), `On:`/`Before:`/`After:` (a date in the budget's format; before and after include the day). Split lines are matched one by one.

post.summary: Start changing the account's email address
post.description: Checks the current password, then emails the current address a link to approve the change; once approved, the new address gets a link to confirm it, and only then does the email change. The answer is the same whether or not the new address already has an account, so it can't be used to find accounts (an address that's taken just never gets a link).

post.summary: Permanently delete the account and its data
post.description: As YNAB does: confirmed with the password (`INVALID_PASSWORD`; attempts share the password-check limit), it deletes every budget the account owns, shared ones included, and removes the account from budgets others shared with it. Logins, sessions, options and two-step verification go too. Can't be undone.

post.description: They get an email with a link that works for 14 days. A budget has at most 6 people, pending invitations included (`BUDGET_FULL`). Someone already in the budget (`ALREADY_MEMBER`) or already invited (`ALREADY_INVITED`) can't be invited.

post.description: On-budget accounts: a null category means Uncategorized; credit-card payment categories can't be used. Tracking accounts never have a category. The payee is matched by name (ignoring case) and created if new; null leaves it empty. `transferAccountId` (instead of `payeeName`) makes it a transfer: a matching transaction with the opposite amount is kept in that account. post.summary: Apply one action to every selected transaction it applies to
post.description: Follows YNAB's action bar: rows an action doesn't apply to are skipped, and `updated` counts the rest. `cleared` skips reconciled rows. `categorize` skips transfers within the budget and tracking-account rows; it un-splits splits, except splits with a transfer line, which stay split with every other line given the category. `memo` replaces the memo (a split's own, not its lines'). `move` moves rows to another account like a single edit (a transfer keeps its other side, which then points at the new account) and skips rows already there, transfers into their own other account and splits with a transfer line to it. `delete` deletes transfers' other sides too and skips the other sides of splits' transfer lines (they go with the split). `duplicate` copies each row as YNAB does: same date and fields, cleared state kept (reconciled becomes cleared), approved, a transfer with a new other side; a split's transfer side copies its whole split, and a transfer selected from both sides is copied once. Rows in (or transferring to) closed accounts are skipped. All of it happens in one database transaction.

patch.summary: Edit a transaction, move it to another account, or toggle cleared
patch.description: On-budget accounts: a null category means Uncategorized; credit-card payment categories can't be used. Tracking accounts never have a category. The payee is matched by name (ignoring case) and created if new; null leaves it empty. `transferAccountId` (instead of `payeeName`) makes it a transfer: a matching transaction with the opposite amount is kept in that account. Only a transfer from a budget account to a tracking account has a category (on the budget side), as money leaves the budget. New transfers need both accounts open. On a transfer, date and amount changes apply to both sides; memo, cleared, flag and category are per side. Setting `payeeName` turns a transfer back into a normal transaction and deletes the other side. A reconciled other side follows and stays reconciled. A reconciled transaction can be edited but stays reconciled, so `cleared` can't be set on it. Moving it to an account that can't use its category resets the category. `subtransactions` (two or more lines, adding up to the amount) splits it across categories; its own `categoryId` is then null. Lines follow the same category and transfer rules. Only budget accounts have splits, and a transfer can't be split (its lines can be transfers). Sending `subtransactions` replaces a split's lines (matched by `id`); changing a split's amount needs new lines too. Giving a split a `categoryId` (or making it a transfer) un-splits it. A split's transfer side only takes memo, cleared, flag and category.
